newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to send troops for Zaire evacuation.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to send troops for Zaire evacuation.

text.p: Belgium plans to send troops to states bordering Zaire for a possible evacuation of Belgians from its troubled former colony, a government official said on Saturday.
The troops will probably be sent to Brazzaville, the capital of Congo, which lies just across the Zaire river from the Zairean capital Kinshasa, he said.
BRTN television said 20 paratroopers would initially be sent to Brazzaville, while 15 would be sent to guard the Belgian embassy in Kinshasa.
"We soon want to have a unit in place for a reconnaissance mission," the official said, adding that Belgium urged all its nationals to leave Zaire as soon as possible.
Belgian media have estimated the number of Europeans in the Zairean capital at about 7,000, including fewer than 3,000 Belgians and about 1,000 French.
On Thursday, France sent extra troops to states neighbouring Zaire, including 90 to Brazzaville, in preparation for a possible evacuation of its citizens.
Zaire is in deep crisis. Longtime ruler President Mobutu Sese Seko, 66, is gravely ill with cancer and rebels led by Laurent Kabila have seized about a fifth of the sprawling central African country.

Since giving Zaire independence in 1960, Belgium has repeatedly sent troops to evacuate nationals during the many crises of Mobutu's regime, most recently in 1993, when 650 paratroopers evacuated nationals from a Kinshasa overrun by rioting Zairean soldiers.
While Belgium cut diplomatic ties with Mobutu in 1990, economic ties with the former colony remain strong, with many Belgian companies active in banking, mining, textile, brewing and cattle-growing.

Analysts say Belgium is well positioned to play a strong role in a post-Mobutu Zaire. Unlike France, which has backed Mobutu after he lost virtually all other Western support, Belgium has distanced itself from his iron-fisted regime.
So far, Belgium has started no official diplomatic relations with new strongman Kabila but has called him a force to be reckoned with.
Most Zairean opposition groups, notably Etienne Tshisekedi's UDPS party, have representations in Brussels.
